books.section: Topic 9.3 The End of the Cold War
Prosperity and a New World Order (1988–2000)

options.text: Germany's capital was divided by a fortified barrier between Communist East and democratic West.

options.misconception: Reunification came in 1990, after the Wall fell; while the Wall stood, the two German states were separate.
options.text: East and West Germany had reunified into a single democratic state with open borders.

options.misconception: Soviet troops stayed in Eastern Europe until the Cold War ended.
options.text: The Soviet Union had withdrawn its troops from Eastern Europe and ended its alliances there.

options.misconception: Berlin became the capital of a united Germany only after reunification in 1990.
options.text: Berlin had become the capital of a united Germany after the two German states merged.

rationales.A:
The photograph shows the Wall itself: a watchtower, guards, and a barrier running through a city. Background: the Wall divided Berlin from 1961 to 1989, with Communist East Berlin on one side and democratic West Berlin on the other.
Everything visible — tower, guards, concrete — is the machinery of that division.
rationales.B: Reunification came in 1990, after the Wall fell. Background: while the Wall stood, the two German states were separate, and this photograph shows the barrier that kept them apart.
rationales.C: Soviet troops stayed in Eastern Europe until the Cold War ended. Background: the guards in the tower are East Germans, but the system they served depended on Soviet power behind it.
rationales.D: Berlin became the capital of a united Germany only after reunification in 1990. Background: while the Wall stood, Bonn was West Germany's capital and East Berlin was East Germany's.
rationales.general:
1. Look at what is actually there. A watchtower, two guards, and a concrete barrier cutting through a city.
2. Ask what the barrier divides. Background: the Wall split Berlin from 1961 to 1989, Communist East from democratic West.
3. Ask what it is not. No open border, no single state, no withdrawal — the photograph shows a division being guarded, not ended.
4. Name it plainly. This is the Cold War made concrete: two systems, one city, a wall between them.
Remember: the Wall was not a border on a map — it was a guarded barrier through a capital.
